summary: Mushie territory (Maï-Ndombe) lies north of the Kasai river between Kwamouth to the south-west and Kutu/Inongo to the north-east. No armed group is reported to control any locality as of late 2026: Mushie town, the territorial seat, and the rural villages of the Mushie, Ntandembelo, Nioki and Banzow Moke health zones are under ordinary state authority, with the PNC and customary chiefs keeping order. The Mobondo (Teke-Yaka) militia, still active in neighbouring Kwamouth in mid-2026 despite official pacification claims and a 2026 peace process, is the main nearby threat, mostly for the villages closest to the Kwamouth border and Kasai river. Web research was unavailable for this run (search budget exhausted, news sites blocked), so the assessment rests on default state presence with medium confidence for Mushie town and low elsewhere.

zones.description: Mushie town (territorial seat, Sacré Coeur health area)
zones.evidence: Seat of the territorial administration with a PNC commissariat and courts; no report of armed-group control. Mobondo violence documented in 2025-2026 centres on southern Kwamouth and Maluku, not Mushie town. Web research was unavailable for this run.

zones.description: Southern/western Mushie villages near the Kasai river and the Kwamouth border: Ndjokele 2, Izeli, Kenya, Ngatoko, Maseke (west)
zones.evidence: Villages closest to Kwamouth, where Mobondo groups still raided in 2026 (RFI); no source found reporting militia presence or control in Mushie territory itself, so ordinary state authority with customary chiefs is assumed. Web research was unavailable for this run.

zones.description: Northern and eastern Mushie villages (Ntandembelo, Banzow Moke, Nioki and northern Mushie health zones): Lobongi, Mbali 2, Mpee, Ikili, Bobala, Ibaa, Ngolo, Ngaliema etc.
zones.evidence: Rural villages far from the Mobondo theatre with no reported armed-group activity; order assumed to rest on PNC posts, territorial administration and customary chiefs. Web research was unavailable for this run.
